The accident, which occurred in Dutse, infront of Shafa Fuel Station in the evening of Sunday, involved trucks conveying gravel, commercial tricycles, private vehicles and other road users, leaving several vehicles damaged and victims trapped or injured.
Although four deaths had been recorded as of the time of filing this report, the identities of the deceased were yet to be established.
Eyewitnesses attributed the accident to the loss of control of one of the trucks conveying gravel, which allegedly rammed into several vehicles, tricycles and pedestrians along the road.
According to some witnesses, the truck driver appeared to have lost control of the heavy-duty vehicle before it crashed into other road users, triggering a chain of collisions involving several vehicles.
The impact of the collision reportedly left multiple vehicles badly damaged, while several persons sustained serious injuries.
One of the eyewitnesses who identified himself as James, expressed fears that the death toll could rise, citing the critical condition of some of the injured victims.
Others said several of those who sustained injuries were in desperate need of medical attention, raising concerns over the possibility of additional casualties.
The incident reportedly caused panic among residents and other road users in the area, as people rushed to assist victims and assess the extent of the destruction.
The involvement of a heavy-duty truck conveying gravel, alongside smaller vehicles and tricycles, reportedly worsened the impact of the crash.
As of the time of filing this report, details surrounding the exact circumstances of the accident, including the number of vehicles involved and the identities of the victims, remained unclear.
There was also no official statement from the Federal Road Safety Cooperation or the police yet on the incident or confirmation of the total number of casualties from the relevant.
The accident has once again drawn attention to concerns over road safety, particularly the dangers posed by heavy-duty vehicles operating alongside commercial tricycles, private motorists and pedestrians on busy roads.
